project_type: React 19 + Vite SPA with Supabase backend (PostgreSQL + Auth + Storage)
language: TypeScript (being migrated from JavaScript; must enable strict mode)
build_system: Vite 6 with React plugin; npm scripts
test_framework: Vitest 1.0+ with React Testing Library and Happy DOM (to be installed)
test_command: npm run test (needs to be added as script in package.json; runs 'vitest')
verification_instructions: After each FEAT: (1) Run `npm run build` and verify no errors; (2) Run `npm run test` for that FEAT's tests and confirm pass; (3) For database changes, verify in Supabase SQL editor by running SELECT queries on new tables/columns; (4) For UI changes, test in browser at http://localhost:5173 using `npm run dev`; (5) For QR codes, test on real mobile devices (iOS and Android) if in staging/production.
snapshot_or_generated_files: Supabase schema changes are one-time SQL migrations (no regeneration needed unless schema reverts). TypeScript types generated from database schema (generate_typescript_types from Supabase, future enhancement). Build outputs: dist/ folder generated by `npm run build`, ignored by git (already in .gitignore).
environment_constraints: Supabase project must be created in advance with email authentication enabled. Environment variables (VITE_SUPABASE_URL, VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, VITE_APP_URL) must be set before QR code testing. VITE_APP_URL must be a public URL (not localhost) for QR codes to work on other devices. Database schema changes are cumulative: run all migrations once on a new Supabase project; do not re-run migrations on same project (will fail or duplicate data). Node.js LTS required.
contribution_requirements: TypeScript strict mode mandatory for all new code. All new functions must have type signatures. React Hook Form + Zod for all forms (no inline validation). TanStack Query for server state management (no direct useState for async data). Supabase RLS policies required for all new tables. Tests required for utilities (80%+ coverage), UI components (60%+ coverage), integration flows. No hardcoded secrets or environment-specific values in code.
key_patterns: Existing patterns in codebase: (1) Supabase client initialized in src/lib/supabase.js, reused throughout; (2) Collections pattern in src/lib/portfolio.js defines tables and fields; (3) Form state managed directly in component state (to be replaced with React Hook Form); (4) RLS policies follow: SELECT visible if owner OR published, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE owner-only; (5) File uploads to storage.objects with path structure: [bucket]/[userId]/[filename]; (6) Error messages shown in 'message' state variable and displayed in flash class; (7) Navigation using React Router; (8) Styling with Tailwind CSS utility classes.
relevant_files: src/lib/supabase.js (Supabase client, rename to .ts and keep exports)
src/pages/Editor.jsx (current flat editor, rewrite as multi-step wizard)
src/pages/Dashboard.jsx (to be enhanced with quick actions)
package.json (dependencies and scripts to be updated)
directory_structure: src/ contains main app code: components/ (Auth, Layout, Protected, UI components, wizard steps, landing sections, portfolio templates), pages/ (Home, Auth, Dashboard, Editor, PublicPortfolio, QR, Settings, Privacy, Terms, ForgotPassword), lib/ (supabase client, validation schemas, file storage, QR utilities, portfolio helpers), hooks/ (custom React hooks for data fetching and form management), types/ (TypeScript interfaces and types), utils/ (date, string, file utilities), styles/ (CSS). tests/ folder for test setup and integration tests. supabase/ contains schema.sql (database DDL, migrations, RLS policies, triggers).
